observations: Photo 0 shows one derelict red cab-over truck with a tank/vacuum unit on the back, consistent with a sewage/vacuum (honey-sucker) truck.
Truck is heavily rusted, body panels dented and perforated, windshield cracked, cab door damaged, no visible tires on rear axle area, sitting on bare dirt.
Background shows what may be another piece of yellow equipment (possibly an excavator arm) but it is out of focus and not identifiable.
No photos at all of the other 10 claimed items: flatbed, mini dumper, CAT backhoe, mini excavator, JCB backhoe, concrete mixer, CAT forklift, Octella crane, 35-ton crane, mobile concrete mixer.
No weighbridge tickets, site-wide photo, or documentation of the claimed 225-ton total shown.
No brand plates, VINs, or model tags legible anywhere in the single photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the truck but no scale or weighbridge ticket to confirm 45 tons.
Only one item of eleven is shown; aggregate weight cannot be checked against any documentation or weighbridge slip.

risks.risk: Ten of eleven listed items (including two cranes, two backhoes, an excavator, forklift, and mixers) have zero photographic evidence of existing at all.
risks.proof: Individual photos or a walk-around video of each of the ten unphotographed items, taken at the stated Port Harcourt site, with some contemporaneous time/location marker (e.g. newspaper, dated signage).
risks.if_unproven: priced as if those ten items do not exist; only the single photographed truck is priced, as scrap-condition weight unconfirmed

risks.risk: Claimed tonnages for every item cannot be checked remotely and heavily inflate the apparent value of the lot.
risks.proof: Certified weighbridge tickets for each unit or the whole lot.
risks.if_unproven: priced at conservative scrap-metal estimate by visible size/condition only, not at claimed tonnage

risks.risk: The truck shown is in advanced disrepair (rust-through panels, broken glass, missing parts) and may not be a runner or even towable, affecting value as scrap vs. working plant.
risks.proof: Photo/video of engine bay, chassis underside, and confirmation of whether it can be started or moved under its own power.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-running scrap metal weight only, not as a functioning vehicle

risks.risk: No proof of seller's ownership or legal right to sell an industrial lot of this scale (no title documents, no company name/registration visible).
risks.proof: Photo of ownership/title documents, business registration, or government disposal certificate (if ex-government scrap).
risks.if_unproven: transaction risk treated as high; no price should be committed until ownership is shown

risks.risk: Classic pattern of a large multi-item industrial scrap claim backed by a single low-information photo is common in advance-fee scrap/equipment scams in Nigeria.
risks.proof: On-the-ground, buyer-commissioned inspection of the full site listing all eleven items side by side.
risks.if_unproven: treated as unconfirmed lot; no price assigned to the unphotographed 90%+ of claimed inventory

proof_requests: Individual clear photos (or a single walk-through video) of every one of the ten unphotographed items, taken together at the same yard as the truck in photo 0.
Weighbridge tickets or any tonnage documentation for the heaviest items (cranes, excavator).
Proof of seller's ownership/title or authorization to sell the lot.
Wider establishing photo of the yard showing multiple items together to confirm they coexist at one site.
response.reason: A claimed 225-ton, eleven-item heavy-equipment lot (including two cranes) is backed by only a single photo of one derelict truck, with no visual or documentary evidence for the other ten items; this gross mismatch between claim scale and evidence is a strong hallmark of a scrap/equipment advance-fee scam pattern.
